ticket.summary: Active water pouring through dining room ceiling light fixture from suspected upstairs bathroom leak; customer shut house main and leak stopped, on-call plumber dispatched to 31 Halcyon Ct.
mitigation_advice: Shut off the house main (found in garage near water heater) - wheel clockwise / lever perpendicular to pipe [PB-02]
Open the lowest cold tap (basement sink) to drain pressure from the lines [PB-03]
Stay clear of sagging water-heavy ceiling and do not operate the affected light switch/fixture [PB-08]
Offered alternative: close the oval supply-line shutoff under the upstairs fixture, clockwise until snug [PB-01]
Keep all water off in the house while waiting for the technician [PB-02]
ticket.customer_message: No need - with the main off, the whole house is depressurized, so the upstairs fixtures can't feed the leak. Just keep all water off, leave the basement tap open to finish draining [PB-03], and stay out from under the wet ceiling and away from that light fixture [PB-08]. You're all set, Maria - on-call plumber is paged and dispatched to 31 Halcyon Ct now, ETA roughly 60-90 minutes; he'll text when he's close. Only charge confirmed tonight is the $150 after-hours dispatch fee, and he'll quote the repair once he finds the source. You did the hard part by getting that main shut off.
